Lowcountry Inshore Grand Slam

Charleston and the South Carolina Lowcountry

THE LOCAL MEANING

What it is.

This South Carolina guide defines the objective as redfish, speckled trout, and flounder. CCA South Carolina uses “inshore grand slam” for that trio. Other regional accounts add black drum. The full Lowcountry title is an editorial regional label, so always state the species when you ask for this trip.

How it is fished.

Live bait, soft plastics, or flies.

The research describes live bait, soft plastics, and flies in Lowcountry creeks. Ask how the captain will divide the tide between targets and what will change if water clarity or access rules out a method. The evidence supports a fall opportunity, not a guaranteed three-species day. It does not establish the same definition throughout Georgia.

Planning format: Half day or full day; inshore skiff. Confirm the actual duration with the provider.

EDITORIAL PREPARATION ADVICE

What to bring.

  • Polarized glasses and sun coverage for shallow-water work.
  • A light rain or wind layer and a small dry bag.
  • Fly or spinning equipment only after the guide confirms the target order and presentation.

Words from this water.

specks ↗
Speckled trout, the local name for spotted seatrout in this saltwater context.
slam ↗
An objective involving a stated group of species; the definition varies by place.
tailing ↗
A fish feeds with its tail visible above shallow water; an observation, not a catch promise.

Before you go.

Does every Lowcountry grand slam include black drum?

No. The sources differ. This page uses redfish, speckled trout, and flounder, while some regional accounts add black drum. Ask the guide to state the intended list.

What seasonal window does the evidence support?

Fall is a documented local window. A seasonal account does not confirm current availability. Use the linked authority for current rules.

What must I confirm before I book this trip?

Agree on whether the slam has three species or includes black drum. Confirm bait, flies or lures, rods, and release equipment. Ask which creek or sound, tide window, and departure point the trip uses. Castward has no confirmed guide inventory for this trip type.
